newsitem.title: USA: Conn. wants to choose pay phone providers in state.
newsitem.headline: Conn. wants to choose pay phone providers in state.

text.p: Connecticut officials said Thursday they want the state rather than federal regulators to decide who can operate pay phones in Connecticut.

Attorney General Richard Blumenthal and Department of Public Utility Control Chairman Reginald Smith said they have urged the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to reconsider a decision to allow private pay phone companies in the state.
The only pay phone operator at present in Connecticut is New Haven-based Southern New England Telecommunications Corp.
Under state rules, only companies that provide local exchange service can provide pay phones in the state.
AT&T Corp is providing local exchange service in Connecticut.

"The Commission should reconsider its (December 1996) decision preempting DPUC's authority to protect consumers from abusive practices in the provision of pay phone services," the state's petition to the FCC said.

"We are urging the FCC to reconsider this ruling, which very simply will expose consumers to outrageous charges of $10 to $15 for one-minute calls," it continued. "We are very hopeful that the FCC will not stop Connecticut from its very legitimate efforts to protect consumers."
